clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old male presented with worsening right upper extremity weakness and numbness, burning pain, and hand swelling, suggestive of brachial plexopathy. A CT scan of the chest revealed a right apical mass extending to the right supraclavicular region. A CT-guided biopsy of this mass confirmed non-small cell lung carcinoma. Immunohistochemistry further classified the tumor as squamous cell carcinoma, showing expression of CK5, p63, and p40, and negativity for TTF1, synaptophysin, and chromogranin.
